title: Inference pipeline weekly scrapbook — kernel & cache notes
content:
Week: 2026-11-23 -> 2026-11-27
Owners: Asha (owner), Jon (kernels), Sana (kv cache), Luis (batching heuristics)
Context: quick, messy weekly ledger for the serving-runtime subteam focused on three active threads: kernel selection and regressions, KV cache prefill/eviction adjustments, and batching heuristics for mixed-length traffic. Aim: capture what we tried, rough numbers, live blockers, and followups.

1) Standup highlights (Mon/Tue/Wed notes consolidated)
- Mon: noticed a 7% tail increase at p99 on host-32 at 09:30–11:00 UTC after rolling runtime v1.9.3. Jon bisected to kernel-memcopy tweak in PR #1842. Reverted the memcopy micro-optim and tail restored.
- Tue: Sana instrumented KV cache warmup telemetry (sampled traces + hitrate per-route). Early signals show prefix-healing decreased cold-start latency by 9% for chat endpoints with short histories.
- Wed: Luis ran a quick sim of dynamic micro-batching on a replay trace; found a 6% throughput regression when coalescing > 8 short requests into one batch for gpt-2-medium family models (likely NVTX contention in kernel library).

2) Experiments and quick results
- Kernel experiment: memory copy path A vs B (PR 1842 revert + A/B toggle). Results across 3 runs: p50 unchanged, p95 +3%, p99 +7% for path B under load. Action: keep default = A, create micro-benchmark to isolate vector-copy latency and scheduler interference. Owner: Jon.
- KV prefill heuristic: enabled per-route 10s lookback prefetch for routes with >500 req/day. Observed hitrate delta: baseline 38% -> prefill 62% after 30m warmup. Latency reduction on cold-start median ~-22ms, p95 ~-40ms. Note: CPU overhead increased by ~2.4% on controllers due to extra async tasks. Risk: scale cost. Owner: Sana.
- Batching coalescer tuning: switched to adaptive-window with soft cap 16 tokens and weight on arrival-time. Replay run (3h): average tokens/batch up 12% but tail latency p99 worsened by 5% in high-concurrency windows. Hypothesis: contention at CUDA stream submission when many small batches flush concurrently. Next step: try batching flush jitter + limited parallelism on stream submission. Owner: Luis.

3) Metrics snapshot (approx, internal sampling)
- Baseline: hosted/region-us-east-1, peak sim load 4200 rps, model family rex-7b-16k
- Median generation latency: 34ms (tokens only)
- p95 generation latency: 102ms
- p99 generation latency: 320ms (up from 300ms after kernel change)
- KV cache hitrate (all routes): 48% -> 58% after aggressive prefill in subset
- Controller CPU: +2.4% with prefill tasks
- Batches per second: +9% with adaptive coalescing, but average batch size plateaued

4) Open blockers / incidents
- Incident: brief customer impact Monday morning; automated rollback worked but rollout process flagged as fragile (rollout tool didn't honor canary fractions for 12m). Assigned to release-eng to harden. Link: JIRA-RT-5121.
- Blocker: lack of deterministic microbench for CUDA stream submission cost (Jon + infra). Need a lightweight harness pinned to specific kernel versions. Without it, kernel perf diffs are noisy.
- Blocker: memory pressure in classifier route when KV prefill runs concurrently with large-batch generation. Observed ephemeral OOM on one host in staging. Action: add soft prefill throttle when GPU memory > 85%.

5) Decisions made
- Revert memcopy micro-optim permanently from runtime v1.9.x until we have microbench evidence that it helps (rollback merged: PR 1850).
- Keep KV prefill gated behind per-customer opt-in for dedicated fleets this week while we gather cost numbers.
- Adopt short-term mitigations for batching-induced tail: introduce jitter on flush + cap concurrent stream submissions to 8 per GPU.

6) Action items (owner — ETA)
- Jon: build CUDA stream submission microbench + run across driver versions (ETA: 2026-12-03).
- Sana: produce cost delta report for prefill task CPU + network (ETA: 2026-11-30).
- Luis: prototype flush-jitter + stream cap in coalescer branch and run replay tests (ETA: 2026-11-29).
- Release Eng: fix rollout fraction bug + postmortem (ETA: 2026-11-28).
- Infra: increase staging host swap temporarily to avoid OOM during simultaneous prefill + large batch replay (ETA: 2026-11-26) — DONE.

7) Notes to self / rough ideas (scratchpad)
- Consider hybrid prefilling: only prefill tokens for last-turn embeddings (cheap) and defer large-history KV writes to background compaction. Might reduce controller CPU.
- Evaluate per-model quantization impact on submission jitter; smaller models trigger less CUDA overhead.
- Try a burst-mode that bypasses coalescer for very short (<=8 token) requests during high concurrency windows to avoid cross-batch contention.

8) Meeting reminders / next sync
- Deep-dive kernel triage — Thu 2026-11-26 10:00 UTC (Jon leads)
- Coalescer tuning review — Fri 2026-11-27 16:00 UTC (Luis leads)

9) Links / refs (quick)
- PRs: github/runtime/pulls/1842, 1850, 1855 (coalescer jitter)
- Replay traces used: s3://replays/2026-11-15/peak-window
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (pinned: kv-prefill-observations)

Unresolved questions to raise in triage:
- Is the CUDA stream contention fundamental at driver level or something we trigger from our submission pattern?
- What is an acceptable controller CPU overhead tradeoff for a 20ms cold-start win?
- Can we safely backlog prefill tasks during off-peak windows for Dedicated customers?

Raw scratch:
- Quick numbers from Tue 11/24 09:00 run: small-batch flush jitter experiment reduced p99 by ~11% when jitter window = 4ms, but throughput hit -1.8%. Worth the trade? TBD.

If you see missing context, add notes here. This is intentionally informal — meant to be a fast capture for the team while we iterate.
